# reminder-producer implementation plan â€” Round 6 (Claude revision)

Responds to Codex round 5 (8.2/10, 4 required changes, all mechanical/precise â€” no new structural
issues found this round, a good convergence signal). Everything from rounds 1-5 not contradicted
here is final.

## Required change 1: placeholder collision fixed

`:now` collides with `occ.ts`'s reserved placeholder (`occ.ts:85,96`, throws on collision per
`occ.ts:130` â€” confirmed by re-reading). Fixed: the checkpoint's `extraConditions` entry uses
`:leaseNow` instead, and â€” since `leaseUntil` is persisted as an ISO string (consistent with
`GSI6SK`'s existing `<leaseUntil-ISO>#...` sort-key design from round 4's reconciliation pointer,
confirmed against that shape) â€” the comparison value is `new Date().toISOString()`, not
`Date.now()`: `extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND leaseUntil >= :leaseNow
AND #cursorCond", values: { ":leaseNow": new Date().toISOString(), ... } }]`. ISO-8601 timestamps
compare correctly lexicographically (same property this codebase's other ISO-sortable keys, e.g.
`GSI6SK`, already rely on), so a plain string `>=` DynamoDB condition is sound without any numeric
conversion.

## Required change 2: continuation event carries a COMPLETE `SqsCommandEnvelope` in `data`, matching the existing dispatch pattern exactly

Codex's finding, verified: `DispatchOutboxRelay` does NOT wrap `event.data` into an
`SqsCommandEnvelope` â€” it forwards `record.payload` (i.e. `event.data`) to the destination's sender
as-is (`relay.ts:91`, `composition/reminder.ts:140-144`). Today's dispatch path only works because
`producer.ts` builds the COMPLETE `DispatchCommand` (`messageVersion`, `messageId`, `commandType`,
`tenantId`, `deduplicationKey`, `data`, `producer.ts:246-262`) and assigns it directly as
`event.data` (`producer.ts:284`, `command as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`) â€” the event's
`data` field IS the wire message, not a wrapper around it. This plan's continuation event follows
the IDENTICAL shape, corrected from round 4/5's "inner fields only" mistake:

```ts
const continuationCommand: SqsCommandEnvelope<{
  shardFnVersion: number; shardId: number; minute: string;
  ownerToken: string; lastEvaluatedKey?: Record<string, unknown>; rolloutEpoch: number;
}> = {
  messageVersion: 1,
  messageId: deps.newEventId(),
  commandType: "reminder.scan-continuation.v1",
  createdAt: now,
  correlationId,
  tenantId: "SYSTEM",
  deduplicationKey: `${shardFnVersion}|${shardId}|${minuteISO}|${pagesProcessed + 1}`,
  data: { shardFnVersion, shardId, minute: minuteISO, ownerToken, lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey, rolloutEpoch: currentEpoch },
};
const event: DomainEvent = { specVersion: "1.0", eventId: deps.newEventId(), eventType: "reminder.scan-continuation.v1", source: "expiration-tracker.reminder-producer", occurredAt: now, correlationId, tenantId: "SYSTEM", actor: { type: "SYSTEM" }, aggregate: { type: "ReminderScanLease", id: `${shardFnVersion}#${shardId}#${minuteISO}`, version: newLeaseVersion }, data: continuationCommand as unknown as Record<string, unknown> };
```
`schemas/events/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json`'s `data` sub-schema is corrected to describe
this FULL `SqsCommandEnvelope` shape (not just the inner fields) â€” effectively
`allOf: [{"$ref": "../queues/command-envelope.v1.json"}, {"properties": {"commandType": {"const":
"reminder.scan-continuation.v1"}, "tenantId": {"const": "SYSTEM"}, "data": {"required": [...,
"rolloutEpoch"], "properties": {..., "rolloutEpoch": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1}}}}}]`
nested inside the outer `domain-event-envelope.v1.json`'s own `data: {"type": "object"}` slot â€”
i.e. the event schema's `data` property is now `{"allOf": [{"$ref":
"../queues/command-envelope.v1.json"}, {...as above...}]}` rather than a flat field list. The
QUEUE-side schema (`schemas/queues/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json`, what the claim/scan
consumer actually validates against on receipt) is now identical in shape to this embedded `data`
description â€” both describe the exact same wire bytes, since no relay-side transformation happens
between them (this is what makes the "mirrors" language from round 5 concrete rather than
hand-wavy: they're not just similar, they're validating the identical object).

## Required change 3: `rolloutEpoch` â€” required, present everywhere a start/continuation is emitted

Added to BOTH schemas' `required` arrays (event-side and queue-side, both corrected above).
**Every emitter of a start or continuation message stamps it**, named explicitly: (a) the
EventBridge-triggered enumeration's fresh-acquire path, (b) the reclaim path (both the
EventBridge-tick reclaim AND, critically per Codex's specific catch, reminder-reconciliation's new
`SCANLEASE` reclaim pass â€” round 4/5 hadn't named this second reclaim site as an epoch-stamping
site, now explicit: `runReconciliation`'s new pass reads the SAME `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` environment
variable, requiring reconciliation's Lambda config to also carry it, one more env var on an
existing function), and (c) the checkpoint path (carries forward the SAME epoch the invocation
itself was invoked under â€” read once from its own environment at cold start, not re-read per
message, so a long-lived warm invocation spanning an epoch bump still finishes its in-flight page
under the OLD epoch consistently rather than mixing epochs mid-page â€” acceptable since the 90s
quiescence wait, Â§4, guarantees no such invocation survives across a real rollback/roll-forward
cycle anyway).

## Required change 4: rollback/roll-forward ordering â€” explicit gates, not implied sequencing

**Rollback**, restated as a strict, named sequence:
1. Terraform apply: both event-source-mappings' `enabled = false`.
2. **Gate**: poll `aws lambda get-event-source-mapping` (via the `claude-dev` profile, per this
   repo's existing AWS-verification convention) for BOTH mappings until `State == "Disabled"`
   (AWS's own documented terminal state, distinct from the transitional `Disabling` â€” confirmed
   via AWS Lambda's `UpdateEventSourceMapping`/`GetEventSourceMapping` API reference this round,
   Codex's own citation). Do NOT start the quiescence timer on apply-success alone.
3. **Gate**: 90-second bounded wait (unchanged number/reasoning from round 5) starts only after
   step 2's poll confirms both `Disabled`.
4. Terraform apply: `SCAN_MODE = "LEGACY"`.

**Roll-forward** (new/re-enable â€” not previously given its own explicit gate order, added this
round): 1. Terraform apply: bump `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` to `N+1` (deployed as a Lambda environment
variable change, same mechanism as `SCAN_MODE` itself) â€” this MUST land before step 2, so anything
that starts matching from step 2 onward is unambiguously post-bump. 2. Terraform apply:
`SCAN_MODE = "PAGED"`. 3. Terraform apply: both mappings' `enabled = true`. Any message left queued
from before the rollback (necessarily stamped with epoch â‰¤ N, since nothing could stamp `N+1`
before step 1 completed) is now provably stale the instant a handler reads it under the new
`SCAN_MODE_EPOCH = N+1` â€” closing required change 3's residual-message concern with the exact
ordering guarantee Codex asked for, not just the comparison mechanism alone.

## Self-grade (Claude, blind â€” before seeing Codex round 6)

**9.3/10.** All 4 fixes are narrow, mechanical, and each traces to a specific Codex citation with
no new structural surface introduced (round 5's own critique confirmed 3 of 4 items were
"conceptually closed, integration incomplete" â€” this round is exactly that integration, not a new
idea). The one piece I'd flag as still worth a skeptical read: the `data.data` nesting in the event
schema (an `SqsCommandEnvelope` embedded inside a `DomainEvent`'s `data` field, itself containing
ANOTHER `data`) is verbose and easy to get subtly wrong in a real Ajv schema file â€” it's correct by
construction (matches `producer.ts`'s own existing double-nesting exactly) but worth the
implementer writing the actual schema file carefully rather than trusting this doc's prose
one-for-one.

   63: interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {

   73: /**
   74:  * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
   75:  * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
   76:  * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see

   78:  * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
   79:  * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
   80:  * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
   81:  * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
   82:  * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
   83:  */
   84: function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
   85:   const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
   86: 
   87:   const names: Record<string, string> = {
   88:     "#version": "version",
   89:     [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
   90:     "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
   91:   };
   92:   const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
   93:     ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
   94:     [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
   95:     ":one": 1,
   96:     ":now": now,
   97:   };
   98: 
   99:   const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
  100:   let i = 0;
  101:   for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
  102:     const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
  103:     const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
  104:     names[nameKey] = field;
  105:     values[valueKey] = value;
  106:     setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
  107:     i += 1;
  108:   }
  109: 
  110:   const removeClauses: string[] = [];
  111:   let j = 0;
  112:   for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
  113:     const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
  114:     names[nameKey] = field;
  115:     removeClauses.push(nameKey);
  116:     j += 1;
  117:   }
  118: 
  119:   const expression =
  120:     removeClauses.length > 0
  121:       ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
  122:       : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
  123: 
  124:   const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
  125:   for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
  126:     for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
  127:       if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
  128:       names[nameKey] = name;
  129:     }
  130:     for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
  131:       if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
  132:       values[valueKey] = value;
  133:     }
  134:     baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
  135:   }
  136: 
  137:   return {
  138:     TableName: input.tableName,
  139:     Key: input.key,
  140:     UpdateExpression: expression,
  141:     ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
  142:     ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
  143:     ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
  144:   };
  145: }

  200:  * equality condition over specific fields (not a `version` counter) - the pattern
  201:  * `TenantQuotaService`'s `updateConditional`/`putIfAbsent` already use standalone
  202:  * (`identity-store.ts`'s `updateConditional`: full-item PutCommand conditioned on
  203:  * `count`/`resetAt` still matching what was read, not an UpdateItem). Exists so quota's
  204:  * transaction-boundary migration (W3-07 writer inventory) can build the same conditional
  205:  * Put as a `TransactWriteItems` entry via `occ.ts` instead of a hand-written
  206:  * ConditionExpression, per this module's own "never hand-written ConditionExpression"
  207:  * discipline. `names`/`values` follow the same collision-checked merge as
  208:  * `buildVersionedUpdate`'s `extraConditions`.

  268: /**
  269:  * Builds a version-conditioned Delete input (W3-06 purge worker's terminal step - a Document
  270:  * row can only be physically removed if it is still at the exact version/state the claim
  271:  * observed, same OCC discipline as `buildVersionedUpdate`, just for `DeleteItem` instead of
  272:  * `UpdateItem`). `extraConditions` uses the same collision-checked merge as
  273:  * `buildVersionedUpdate` - see that function's docs.
  274:  */
  275: export function buildVersionedDelete(input: {
  276:   tableName: string;
  277:   key: EntityKey;
  278:   tenantId: string;
  279:   expectedVersion: number;
  280:   extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
  281: }): DynamoDeleteCommandInput {
  282:   const names: Record<string, string> = { "#version": "version", "#tenantId": "tenantId" };
  283:   const values: Record<string, unknown> = { ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion, ":tenantId": input.tenantId };
  284:   const conditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", "#tenantId = :tenantId"];
  285: 
  286:   for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
  287:     for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
  288:       if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved key: ${nameKey}`);
  289:       names[nameKey] = name;
  290:     }
  291:     for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
  292:       if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved key: ${valueKey}`);
  293:       values[valueKey] = value;
  294:     }
  295:     conditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
  296:   }
  297: 
  298:   return {
  299:     TableName: input.tableName,
  300:     Key: input.key,
  301:     ConditionExpression: conditionParts.join(" AND "),
  302:     ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
  303:     ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
  304:   };
  305: }
  306: 
  307: /**
  308:  * Sibling of `buildConditionalPut` for `DeleteItem` - symmetric reasoning: `buildVersionedDelete`
  309:  * above always ANDs `#version = :expectedVersion`, which only makes sense for a versioned
  310:  * (mutable) entity. An append-only entity that is NEVER updated after creation (e.g. the
  311:  * `AuditEvent` family - `expiration`/`organization`/`subject`/`activity` modules' audit rows,
  312:  * D-153) has no `version` counter to check at all, so forcing one through `buildVersionedDelete`
  313:  * would require faking a field that does not exist on the row. Callers instead supply their own
  314:  * equality condition over whatever field they observed at scan time (same
  315:  * "hasn't changed since scan" intent as `buildVersionedDelete`'s `extraConditions`, just without
  316:  * a version to anchor it to) - `names`/`values` follow the same collision-free-by-caller-control
  317:  * discipline as `buildConditionalPut` (no generated placeholders to collide with here, since this
  318:  * builder adds none of its own beyond `attribute_exists`).
  319:  */
  320: export function buildConditionalDelete(input: {
  321:   tableName: string;
  322:   key: EntityKey;
  323:   conditionExpression: string;
  324:   names?: Record<string, string>;
  325:   values?: Record<string, unknown>;
  326: }): DynamoDeleteCommandInput {
  327:   return {
  328:     TableName: input.tableName,
  329:     Key: input.key,
  330:     ConditionExpression: input.conditionExpression,
  331:     ExpressionAttributeNames: input.names,
  332:     ExpressionAttributeValues: input.values,
  333:   };
  334: }

  338: /**
  339:  * Builds a TransactWriteItems `ConditionCheck` entry asserting a row is still at an
  340:  * expected version (and, optionally, still holds a given attribute value) - used to fence
  341:  * a commit against a fact read earlier in the same operation but not itself written by
  342:  * this transaction (e.g. reminder dispatch asserting the ReminderPolicy it read is still
  343:  * enabled at the version it read, per the BLOCKER-B freshness-fencing fix: reading a row
  344:  * and later writing elsewhere based on that read is a TOCTOU gap unless the read fact is
  345:  * re-asserted atomically inside the same TransactWriteItems as the write it gates).
  346:  */
  347: export function buildVersionConditionCheck(input: {
  348:   tableName: string;
  349:   key: EntityKey;
  350:   expectedVersion: number;
  351:   /** Extra attribute=value equality conditions beyond version, e.g. { enabled: true, status: "ACTIVE" }. */
  352:   extra?: Record<string, unknown>;
  353: }): TransactConditionCheckEntry {
  354:   const names: Record<string, string> = { "#version": "version" };
  355:   const values: Record<string, unknown> = { ":version": input.expectedVersion };
  356:   const clauses = ["#version = :version"];
  357: 
  358:   let i = 0;
  359:   for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.extra ?? {})) {
  360:     const nameKey = `#c${i}`;
  361:     const valueKey = `:c${i}`;
  362:     names[nameKey] = field;
  363:     values[valueKey] = value;
  364:     clauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
  365:     i += 1;
  366:   }
  367: 
  368:   return {
  369:     ConditionCheck: {
  370:       TableName: input.tableName,
  371:       Key: input.key,
  372:       ConditionExpression: clauses.join(" AND "),
  373:       ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
  374:       ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
  375:     },
  376:   };
  377: }
  378: 
  379: /**
  380:  * Sibling of `buildVersionConditionCheck` for facts that have no version to pin - e.g.
  381:  * BLOCKER-B's ITEM-scoped-policy integrity check (a po…9531 tokens truncated…nantManagerLookup {
   25:   async function isGlobalUserActive(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {

   27:     return (result.Item as { identityStatus?: string } | undefined)?.identityStatus === "ACTIVE";
   28:   }
   29: 
   30:   return {
   31:     async listActiveManagers(tenantId: string): Promise<{ userId: string }[]> {
   32:       const { PK } = organizationKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity({ tenantId }));
   33:       const result = await client.send(new QueryCommand({ TableName: tableName, ConsistentRead: true, KeyConditionExpression: "PK = :pk AND begins_with(SK, :prefix)", ExpressionAttributeValues: { ":pk": PK, ":prefix": "MEMBER#" } }));
   34:       const candidates = ((result.Items ?? []) as Membership[]).filter((m) => m.status === "ACTIVE" && MANAGER_ROLES.has(m.role));
   35:       const activeFlags = await Promise.all(candidates.map((m) => isGlobalUserActive(m.userId)));

   94: /** M10 cluster 4 (D-039/D-046/D-048): `chasingQueueUrl` is optional so this function keeps

  100:  * this same shared relay, same reasoning. */
  101: export function buildOutboxRelayDeps(
  102:   client: DynamoDBDocumentClient,
  103:   tableName: string,
  104:   queueUrl: string,
  105:   sqsClient: SQSClient = new SQSClient({}),
  106:   chasingQueueUrl?: string,
  107:   importCommitQueueUrl?: string,
  108:   materializationTriggerQueueUrl?: string,
  109:   // D-192 slice 9: FOURTH optional sender on this same shared relay - `POST /mapping`'s
  110:   // AWAITING_MAPPING->PARSING transition dispatches this destination in the same TWI as the
  111:   // claim (import-service.ts#submitImportMapping). Same "bare event.data, self-contained"
  112:   // payload shape as SQS_IMPORT_COMMIT_V1 (tenantId embedded, no extra envelope wrapping).
  113:   importParseQueueUrl?: string,
  114:   // D-193 item 6/9: FIFTH optional sender - `confirmFieldForDocumentArchive`/`commitRunOutcome`
  115:   // dispatch this destination in the same TWI as `DocumentVersion`'s `validUntil` Update, only
  116:   // when it actually changed. Same bare-event-data shape as SQS_IMPORT_PARSE_V1 above; the
  117:   // payload's `validUntil` is a mere wake-up hint - requirement-evidence-refresh-handler.ts
  118:   // never trusts it, always re-reads DocumentVersion+Requirement fresh.
  119:   requirementEvidenceRefreshQueueUrl?: string,
  120:   // D-204 fatia 3 (Roadmap P1 item 15): SIXTH optional sender - the scheduled-reports
  121:   // scheduler (D-212) dispatches this destination in the same TWI as its claim `Update` on
  122:   // `ReportSubscription`. Same bare-event-data shape (`runId`/`subscriptionId`/`tenantId`/
  123:   // `scheduledFor`) as the other bare-payload destinations above -
  124:   // report-subscription-delivery-handler.ts never trusts anything beyond those four fields.
  125:   reportSubscriptionDeliveryQueueUrl?: string,
  126:   // D-205 fatia 2 (Roadmap P1 item 16): SEVENTH optional sender -
  127:   // `DocumentArchiveService.confirmDossierExport` dispatches this destination in the same TWI
  128:   // as its `DossierExportRun` status Update (CONFIRMED). Same bare-event-data shape
  129:   // (`runId`/`subjectId`/`tenantId`) as the other bare-payload destinations above.
  130:   dossierExportQueueUrl?: string,
  131:   // D-226 (Roadmap P0 item 9): EIGHTH optional sender - `buildDocumentRequestCreatedOutboxEntry`
  132:   // dispatches this destination in the same TWI that creates/reissues a `DocumentRequest`. Same
  133:   // bare-event-data shape (`tenantId`/`subjectId`/`documentRequestId`/`issuanceGeneration`) as the
  134:   // other bare-payload destinations above - document-request-credential-issuance-handler.ts (the
  135:   // GUEST Lambda, holds the D-146 pepper) never trusts anything beyond those four fields, always
  136:   // re-reads the authoritative DocumentRequest.
  137:   guestCredentialIssuanceQueueUrl?: string,
  138: ) {
  139:   const store = new DynamoDbOutboxRelayStore(client, tableName);
  140:   const send = (targetQueueUrl: string) => async (payload: Record<string, unknown>, correlationId: string) => {
  141:     await sqsClient.send(
  142:       new SendMessageCommand({
  143:         QueueUrl: targetQueueUrl,
  144:         MessageBody: JSON.stringify(payload),
  145:         MessageAttributes: { correlationId: { DataType: "String", StringValue: correlationId } },
  146:       }),
  147:     );
  148:   };
  149:   // BLOCKER-B (reminder-delivery-pipeline.md Â§4): unlike DispatchCommand, this destination's
  150:   // payload is the bare domain event data (matches schemas/events/*.json exactly, no
  151:   // envelope wrapping) - tenantId/eventType aren't embedded in it, so this sender folds them
  152:   // in from the OutboxRecord's own envelope fields before sending, giving the trigger
  153:   // handler a self-contained message it can build a TriggerEvent from without any other
  154:   // context.
  155:   const sendMaterializationTrigger = (targetQueueUrl: string) => async (payload: Record<string, unknown>, correlationId: string, tenantId: string, eventType: string) => {
  156:     await sqsClient.send(
  157:       new SendMessageCommand({
  158:         QueueUrl: targetQueueUrl,
  159:         MessageBody: JSON.stringify({ eventType, tenantId, data: payload }),
  160:         MessageAttributes: { correlationId: { DataType: "String", StringValue: correlationId } },
  161:       }),
  162:     );
  163:   };
  164:   return {
  165:     store,
  166:     now: () => new Date().toISOString(),
  167:     senders: {
  168:       SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1: send(queueUrl),
  169:       ...(chasingQueueUrl ? { SQS_DOCUMENT_CHASING_DISPATCH_V1: send(chasingQueueUrl) } : {}),
  170:       ...(importCommitQueueUrl ? { SQS_IMPORT_COMMIT_V1: send(importCommitQueueUrl) } : {}),
  171:       ...(importParseQueueUrl ? { SQS_IMPORT_PARSE_V1: send(importParseQueueUrl) } : {}),
  172:       ...(requirementEvidenceRefreshQueueUrl ? { SQS_REQUIREMENT_EVIDENCE_REFRESH_V1: send(requirementEvidenceRefreshQueueUrl) } : {}),
  173:       ...(reportSubscriptionDeliveryQueueUrl ? { SQS_REPORT_SUBSCRIPTION_DELIVERY_V1: send(reportSubscriptionDeliveryQueueUrl) } : {}),
  174:       ...(dossierExportQueueUrl ? { SQS_DOSSIER_EXPORT_V1: send(dossierExportQueueUrl) } : {}),
  175:       ...(guestCredentialIssuanceQueueUrl ? { SQS_DOCUMENT_REQUEST_CREDENTIAL_ISSUANCE_V1: send(guestCredentialIssuanceQueueUrl) } : {}),
  176:       ...(materializationTriggerQueueUrl ? { SQS_REMINDER_MATERIALIZATION_TRIGGER_V1: sendMaterializationTrigger(materializationTriggerQueueUrl) } : {}),
  177:     },
  178:   };
  179: }

    1: # reminder-producer implementation plan â€” Round 6 (Claude revision)
    2: 
    3: Responds to Codex round 5 (8.2/10, 4 required changes, all mechanical/precise â€” no new structural
    4: issues found this round, a good convergence signal). Everything from rounds 1-5 not contradicted
    5: here is final.
    6: 
    7: ## Required change 1: placeholder collision fixed
    8: 
    9: `:now` collides with `occ.ts`'s reserved placeholder (`occ.ts:85,96`, throws on collision per
   10: `occ.ts:130` â€” confirmed by re-reading). Fixed: the checkpoint's `extraConditions` entry uses
   11: `:leaseNow` instead, and â€” since `leaseUntil` is persisted as an ISO string (consistent with
   12: `GSI6SK`'s existing `<leaseUntil-ISO>#...` sort-key design from round 4's reconciliation pointer,
   13: confirmed against that shape) â€” the comparison value is `new Date().toISOString()`, not
   14: `Date.now()`: `extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND leaseUntil >= :leaseNow
   15: AND #cursorCond", values: { ":leaseNow": new Date().toISOString(), ... } }]`. ISO-8601 timestamps
   16: compare correctly lexicographically (same property this codebase's other ISO-sortable keys, e.g.
   17: `GSI6SK`, already rely on), so a plain string `>=` DynamoDB condition is sound without any numeric
   18: conversion.
   19: 
   20: ## Required change 2: continuation event carries a COMPLETE `SqsCommandEnvelope` in `data`, matching the existing dispatch pattern exactly
   21: 
   22: Codex's finding, verified: `DispatchOutboxRelay` does NOT wrap `event.data` into an
   23: `SqsCommandEnvelope` â€” it forwards `record.payload` (i.e. `event.data`) to the destination's sender
   24: as-is (`relay.ts:91`, `composition/reminder.ts:140-144`). Today's dispatch path only works because
   25: `producer.ts` builds the COMPLETE `DispatchCommand` (`messageVersion`, `messageId`, `commandType`,
   26: `tenantId`, `deduplicationKey`, `data`, `producer.ts:246-262`) and assigns it directly as
   27: `event.data` (`producer.ts:284`, `command as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`) â€” the event's
   28: `data` field IS the wire message, not a wrapper around it. This plan's continuation event follows
   29: the IDENTICAL shape, corrected from round 4/5's "inner fields only" mistake:
   30: 
   31: ```ts
   32: const continuationCommand: SqsCommandEnvelope<{
   33:   shardFnVersion: number; shardId: number; minute: string;
   34:   ownerToken: string; lastEvaluatedKey?: Record<string, unknown>; rolloutEpoch: number;
   35: }> = {
   36:   messageVersion: 1,
   37:   messageId: deps.newEventId(),
   38:   commandType: "reminder.scan-continuation.v1",
   39:   createdAt: now,
   40:   correlationId,
   41:   tenantId: "SYSTEM",
   42:   deduplicationKey: `${shardFnVersion}|${shardId}|${minuteISO}|${pagesProcessed + 1}`,
   43:   data: { shardFnVersion, shardId, minute: minuteISO, ownerToken, lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey, rolloutEpoch: currentEpoch },
   44: };
   45: const event: DomainEvent = { specVersion: "1.0", eventId: deps.newEventId(), eventType: "reminder.scan-continuation.v1", source: "expiration-tracker.reminder-producer", occurredAt: now, correlationId, tenantId: "SYSTEM", actor: { type: "SYSTEM" }, aggregate: { type: "ReminderScanLease", id: `${shardFnVersion}#${shardId}#${minuteISO}`, version: newLeaseVersion }, data: continuationCommand as unknown as Record<string, unknown> };
   46: ```
   47: `schemas/events/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json`'s `data` sub-schema is corrected to describe
   48: this FULL `SqsCommandEnvelope` shape (not just the inner fields) â€” effectively
   49: `allOf: [{"$ref": "../queues/command-envelope.v1.json"}, {"properties": {"commandType": {"const":
   50: "reminder.scan-continuation.v1"}, "tenantId": {"const": "SYSTEM"}, "data": {"required": [...,
   51: "rolloutEpoch"], "properties": {..., "rolloutEpoch": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1}}}}}]`
   52: nested inside the outer `domain-event-envelope.v1.json`'s own `data: {"type": "object"}` slot â€”
   53: i.e. the event schema's `data` property is now `{"allOf": [{"$ref":
   54: "../queues/command-envelope.v1.json"}, {...as above...}]}` rather than a flat field list. The
   55: QUEUE-side schema (`schemas/queues/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json`, what the claim/scan
   56: consumer actually validates against on receipt) is now identical in shape to this embedded `data`
   57: description â€” both describe the exact same wire bytes, since no relay-side transformation happens
   58: between them (this is what makes the "mirrors" language from round 5 concrete rather than
   59: hand-wavy: they're not just similar, they're validating the identical object).
   60: 
   61: ## Required change 3: `rolloutEpoch` â€” required, present everywhere a start/continuation is emitted
   62: 
   63: Added to BOTH schemas' `required` arrays (event-side and queue-side, both corrected above).
   64: **Every emitter of a start or continuation message stamps it**, named explicitly: (a) the
   65: EventBridge-triggered enumeration's fresh-acquire path, (b) the reclaim path (both the
   66: EventBridge-tick reclaim AND, critically per Codex's specific catch, reminder-reconciliation's new
   67: `SCANLEASE` reclaim pass â€” round 4/5 hadn't named this second reclaim site as an epoch-stamping
   68: site, now explicit: `runReconciliation`'s new pass reads the SAME `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` environment
   69: variable, requiring reconciliation's Lambda config to also carry it, one more env var on an
   70: existing function), and (c) the checkpoint path (carries forward the SAME epoch the invocation
   71: itself was invoked under â€” read once from its own environment at cold start, not re-read per
   72: message, so a long-lived warm invocation spanning an epoch bump still finishes its in-flight page
   73: under the OLD epoch consistently rather than mixing epochs mid-page â€” acceptable since the 90s
   74: quiescence wait, Â§4, guarantees no such invocation survives across a real rollback/roll-forward
   75: cycle anyway).
   76: 
   77: ## Required change 4: rollback/roll-forward ordering â€” explicit gates, not implied sequencing
   78: 
   79: **Rollback**, restated as a strict, named sequence:
   80: 1. Terraform apply: both event-source-mappings' `enabled = false`.
   81: 2. **Gate**: poll `aws lambda get-event-source-mapping` (via the `claude-dev` profile, per this
   82:    repo's existing AWS-verification convention) for BOTH mappings until `State == "Disabled"`
   83:    (AWS's own documented terminal state, distinct from the transitional `Disabling` â€” confirmed
   84:    via AWS Lambda's `UpdateEventSourceMapping`/`GetEventSourceMapping` API reference this round,
   85:    Codex's own citation). Do NOT start the quiescence timer on apply-success alone.
   86: 3. **Gate**: 90-second bounded wait (unchanged number/reasoning from round 5) starts only after
   87:    step 2's poll confirms both `Disabled`.
   88: 4. Terraform apply: `SCAN_MODE = "LEGACY"`.
   89: 
   90: **Roll-forward** (new/re-enable â€” not previously given its own explicit gate order, added this
   91: round): 1. Terraform apply: bump `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` to `N+1` (deployed as a Lambda environment
   92: variable change, same mechanism as `SCAN_MODE` itself) â€” this MUST land before step 2, so anything
   93: that starts matching from step 2 onward is unambiguously post-bump. 2. Terraform apply:
   94: `SCAN_MODE = "PAGED"`. 3. Terraform apply: both mappings' `enabled = true`. Any message left queued
   95: from before the rollback (necessarily stamped with epoch â‰¤ N, since nothing could stamp `N+1`
   96: before step 1 completed) is now provably stale the instant a handler reads it under the new
   97: `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH = N+1` â€” closing required change 3's residual-message concern with the exact
   98: ordering guarantee Codex asked for, not just the comparison mechanism alone.
   99: 
  100: ## Self-grade (Claude, blind â€” before seeing Codex round 6)
  101: 
  102: **9.3/10.** All 4 fixes are narrow, mechanical, and each traces to a specific Codex citation with
  103: no new structural surface introduced (round 5's own critique confirmed 3 of 4 items were
  104: "conceptually closed, integration incomplete" â€” this round is exactly that integration, not a new
  105: idea). The one piece I'd flag as still worth a skeptical read: the `data.data` nesting in the event
  106: schema (an `SqsCommandEnvelope` embedded inside a `DomainEvent`'s `data` field, itself containing
  107: ANOTHER `data`) is verbose and easy to get subtly wrong in a real Ajv schema file â€” it's correct by
  108: construction (matches `producer.ts`'s own existing double-nesting exactly) but worth the
  109: implementer writing the actual schema file carefully rather than trusting this doc's prose
  110: one-for-one.

   23:    * GSI6PK/GSI6SK when a reconciliation-candidate pointer (M3.5) stops applying. Gap noted
   24:    * since M3 (occ.ts was SET-only, cancelled GSI3 pointers were left orphaned because

   26:    * actively queried by reconciliation. */

   29:   /** Extra ConditionExpression clauses ANDed to the base condition, each with its own
   30:    * caller-supplied names/values (W3-06 purge worker's claim/fence conditions - e.g. checking
   31:    * `legalHold`/`GSI6PK`/`purgeAfter` atomically alongside the version check). Each entry's
   32:    * `expression` is wrapped in its own parentheses before being ANDed in, so callers never need
   33:    * to hand-balance parens against the base condition. Placeholder names/values MUST NOT collide
   34:    * with the base condition's (#version/#tenantId/#updatedAt/:expectedVersion/:tenantId/:one/:now)
   35:    * or with any `set`/`remove` generated key (#set<i>/:set<i>/#rem<j>) - buildVersionedUpdate
   36:    * throws before building an invalid ConditionExpression rather than silently overwriting one
   37:    * caller's placeholder with another's. */
   38:   extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;

   63: interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
   64:   tableName: string;
   65:   key: EntityKey;
   66:   expectedVersion: number;
   67:   set: Record<string, unknown>;
   68:   remove?: string[];
   69:   now?: string;
   70:   extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
   71: }
   72: 
   73: /**
   74:  * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
   75:  * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
   76:  * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
   77:  * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
   78:  * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
   79:  * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
   80:  * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
   81:  * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
   82:  * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
   83:  */
   84: function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
   85:   const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
   86: 
   87:   const names: Record<string, string> = {
   88:     "#version": "version",
   89:     [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
   90:     "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
   91:   };
   92:   const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
   93:     ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
   94:     [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
   95:     ":one": 1,
   96:     ":now": now,
   97:   };
   98: 
   99:   const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
  100:   let i = 0;
  101:   for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
  102:     const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
  103:     const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
  104:     names[nameKey] = field;
  105:     values[valueKey] = value;
  106:     setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
  107:     i += 1;
  108:   }
  109: 
  110:   const removeClauses: string[] = [];
  111:   let j = 0;
  112:   for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
  113:     const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
  114:     names[nameKey] = field;
  115:     removeClauses.push(nameKey);
  116:     j += 1;
  117:   }
  118: 
  119:   const expression =
  120:     removeClauses.length > 0
  121:       ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
  122:       : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
  123: 
  124:   const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
  125:   for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
  126:     for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
  127:       if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
  128:       names[nameKey] = name;
  129:     }
  130:     for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
  131:       if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
  132:       values[valueKey] = value;
  133:     }
  134:     baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
  135:   }
  136: 
  137:   return {
  138:     TableName: input.tableName,
  139:     Key: input.key,
  140:     UpdateExpression: expression,
  141:     ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
  142:     ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
  143:     ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
  144:   };
  145: }
  146: 
  147: /**
  148:  * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
  149:  * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
  150:  * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
  151:  * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
  152:  * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
  153:  */
  154: export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
  155:   return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
  156: }

  417: /** Name of the AWS SDK error thrown when any entry in a TransactWriteItems call fails its
  418:  * ConditionExpression - used by callers to distinguish OCC/idempotency conflicts from other
  419:  * DynamoDB errors without importing the SDK type. */
  420: export const TRANSACTION_CANCELED = "TransactionCanceledException";
  421: 
  422: export function isTransactionCanceled(err: unknown): boolean {
  423:   return (
  424:     typeof err === "object" &&
  425:     err !== null &&
  426:     "name" in err &&
  427:     (err as { name?: unknown }).name === TRANSACTION_CANCELED
  428:   );
  429: }
  430: 
  431: /**
  432:  * Reads the per-item `CancellationReasons` array off a `TransactionCanceledException` (verify
  433:  * with `isTransactionCanceled` first) - the real AWS SDK error carries one entry per transact
  434:  * item, each with a `Code` ("None" for an item that did not cause the cancellation,
  435:  * "ConditionalCheckFailed" for one that did). Wave B2B-5 (D-095, Codex Rodada 3 achado): a
  436:  * `TransactWriteItems` with more than one conditioned entry must never collapse "the
  437:  * transaction was canceled" into "MY condition specifically failed" - a caller distinguishing,
  438:  * say, a cap-guard `Update` at index 0 from an unrelated `Put` collision at index 2 needs the
  439:  * reason for the SPECIFIC index it cares about, not just the fact that something failed.
  440:  * Returns `undefined` (never throws) for any error shape that doesn't carry this array - callers
  441:  * fall back to treating the cancellation as "index unknown" rather than guessing.
  442:  */
  443: export function getCancellationReasonCodes(err: unknown): string[] | undefined {
  444:   if (typeof err !== "object" || err === null || !("CancellationReasons" in err)) return undefined;
  445:   const reasons = (err as { CancellationReasons?: unknown }).CancellationReasons;
  446:   if (!Array.isArray(reasons)) return undefined;
  447:   return reasons.map((reason) => (typeof reason === "object" && reason !== null && "Code" in reason ? String((reason as { Code?: unknown }).Code) : "Unknown"));
  448: }
  449: 
  450: /**
  451:  * Builds an UpdateItem input for a narrow, single-purpose guard write: set one attribute exactly
  452:  * once, gated on it not already existing - no `version` counter, no `tenantId` condition (unlike
  453:  * `buildVersionedUpdate`, whose reserved condition requires `tenantId` and is therefore unusable
  454:  * for a genuinely tenantless entity). Wave B2B-5 (D-095, Codex Rodada 2/3 achado): `GlobalUser`
  455:  * (identity/persistence/global-user-repository.ts) is tenantless, so its
  456:  * `hasCreatedOrganization` cap flag needs this instead. Not a general-purpose OCC update - an
  457:  * entity that needs real optimistic concurrency later should get its own tenantless variant of
  458:  * `buildVersionedUpdate`, not a generalization of this narrow helper.
  459:  */
  460: export function buildAttributeOnceUpdate(input: { tableName: string; key: EntityKey; attribute: string; value: unknown }): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
  461:   return {
  462:     TableName: input.tableName,
  463:     Key: input.key,
  464:     UpdateExpression: "SET #attr = :value",
  465:     ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(#attr)",
  466:     ExpressionAttributeNames: { "#attr": input.attribute },
  467:     ExpressionAttributeValues: { ":value": input.value },
  468:   };
  469: }

  471: /** Name of the AWS SDK error thrown when a ConditionExpression fails - used by callers
  472:  * to distinguish OCC conflicts from other DynamoDB errors without importing the SDK type. */
  473: export const CONDITIONAL_CHECK_FAILED = "ConditionalCheckFailedException";
  474: 
  475: export function isConditionalCheckFailed(err: unknown): boolean {
  476:   return (
  477:     typeof err === "object" &&
  478:     err !== null &&
  479:     "name" in err &&
  480:     (err as { name?: unknown }).name === CONDITIONAL_CHECK_FAILED
  481:   );
  482: }

    7:  * Steps (Â§9.3):

   10:  *     5 minutes) - "sem lookback, 'o prÃ³ximo tick reprocessa' Ã© falso";

   71: export interface ProducerDeps {
   72:   store: ReminderProducerStore;
   73:   shardConfig: ShardConfig;
   74:   tableName: string;
   75:   now: () => string;
   76:   /** Short claim TTL - default 2 minutes, comfortably longer than one producer tick (1 minute) but short enough that a crashed dispatch worker's claim is reclaimable quickly by reconciliation (Â§9.5). */
   77:   claimTtlMs?: number;
   78:   /**
   79:    * Lookback window in minutes, inclusive of the current minute (implementation-blueprint.md
   80:    * Â§9.3 example: [M-5min, M]). Default raised from 5 to 15 (PERF-12 1k load test,
   81:    * docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md): under a realistic
   82:    * burst (many occurrences due the same minute) the producer's 10s timeout could be
   83:    * exceeded for several consecutive minutes, and any occurrence still SCHEDULED once its
   84:    * minute aged out of a 5-minute lookback was never reconciled by any other pass (see
   85:    * reconciliation.ts's own file header - CLAIMS reconciliation only reverts already-CLAIMED
   86:    * occurrences, DST reconciliation only re-materializes missing ones; neither covers
   87:    * "SCHEDULED, past lookback, never claimed"). 15 minutes gives roughly 2x margin over the
   88:    * observed 7-minute burst-recovery window, at a bounded extra cost (shardCount Ã—
   89:    * lookbackMinutes extra GSI3 partition queries per NORMAL tick, most of them empty) - a
   90:    * dedicated reconciliation pass for this case was considered but rejected: GSI3 query
   91:    * access is deliberately isolated to ONLY this worker (reminder-store.ts's own doc comment,
   92:    * enforced by test/integration/gsi3-isolation.test.ts and infra/main.tf's "the ONLY
   93:    * function granted gsi3_read" policy comment) - widening the SAME worker's own lookback,
   94:    * combined with the timeout raise and the parallelism below (both fix the actual cause,
   95:    * this is the safety net), stays inside that existing boundary instead of punching a new
   96:    * hole in it.

   99:   /** Deterministic-in-tests ID generator for the durable outbox event written in the same
  100:    * transaction as the claim (M3.5 "DecisÃ£o central: outbox durÃ¡vel" - see runProducerTick). */
  101:   newEventId: () => string;
  102:   correlationId: () => string;
  103: }

  105: export interface ProducerTickResult {
  106:   claimed: DispatchCommand[];
  107:   /** M10 cluster 4: DocumentChasingOccurrence claims from the SAME GSI3 scan, kept in a
  108:    * separate array (different command shape) - never merged into `claimed`. */
  109:   chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[];
  110:   failed: { occurrenceId: string; tenantId: string; error: unknown }[];
  111:   /** GSI3SK shape matched neither the reminder nor the chasing pattern - fail-closed, never
  112:    * processed. Should always be 0 in practice; a nonzero count is alarm-worthy (D-039). */
  113:   unknownEntityType: number;
  114:   scanned: number;
  115:   minutesScanned: string[];
  116:   shardPartitionsScanned: number;
  117: }
  118: 
  119: function minuteFloor(d: Date): Date {
  120:   return new Date(Math.floor(d.getTime() / 60_000) * 60_000);
  121: }
  122: 
  123: /**
  124:  * PERF-12 1k load test finding (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
  125:  * this loop used to process one occurrence at a time - one `store.get` + one
  126:  * `store.transactWrite` per occurrence, fully sequential - inside a Lambda with (at the time)
  127:  * a 10s timeout. With ~250 occurrences concentrated in one shard/minute under a realistic
  128:  * burst, that budget was nowhere near enough, the function was killed mid-loop repeatedly, and
  129:  * occurrences that hadn't been claimed yet eventually aged out of the lookback window,
  130:  * permanently stuck in SCHEDULED. Bounded concurrency here mirrors the exact pattern already
  131:  * used for the same reason in reminder-dispatch-handler.ts (D-170) - each occurrence's own
  132:  * `transactWrite` stays a single, independent atomic conditional claim (never merged across
  133:  * occurrences), so parallelizing here does not touch the transactional or idempotency
  134:  * guarantees of any individual claim, only how many claims run concurrently. A plain numeric
  135:  * constant, not unbounded `Promise.all`, to keep the burst of concurrent DynamoDB round trips
  136:  * per invocation predictable.
  137:  */
  138: const PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY = 8;
  139: 
  140: /**
  141:  * Pure alarm decision, extracted so the Lambda handler's "when should this tick throw" logic
  142:  * is unit-testable without mocking the whole handler/composition root (achado real de revisÃ£o
  143:  * adversarial, D-039/D-046/D-048: an earlier version of this fail-closed path was silently
  144:  * absorbed by the handler - `unknownEntityType` was counted but nothing ever read it). Two
  145:  * independent reasons, checked in this order for a stable, deterministic message:
  146:  * unrecognized GSI3SK shape (fail-closed, never a retry-race) first, then genuine per-occurrence
  147:  * claim failures.
  148:  */
  149: export function shouldAlarm(result: ProducerTickResult): { alarm: boolean; reason?: string } {
  150:   if (result.unknownEntityType > 0) {
  151:     return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.unknownEntityType} GSI3 row(s) matched neither the reminder nor the chasing entityType - fail-closed` };
  152:   }
  153:   if (result.failed.length > 0) {
  154:     return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.failed.length} occurrence(s) failed to claim` };
  155:   }
  156:   return { alarm: false };
  157: }
  158: 
  159: /** Runs one producer tick for wall-clock minute `tickMinute` (already floored to the minute by the caller/Lambda trigger). */
  160: export async function runProducerTick(deps: ProducerDeps, tickMinute: Date): Promise<ProducerTickResult> {
  161:   const generations = activeGenerations(deps.shardConfig, deps.now());
  162:   const lookback = deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15;
  163:   const claimTtlMs = deps.claimTtlMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
  164: 
  165:   const minutesToScan: Date[] = [];
  166:   for (let i = lookback; i >= 0; i--) {
  167:     minutesToScan.push(minuteFloor(new Date(tickMinute.getTime() - i * 60_000)));
  168:   }
  169: 
  170:   const claimed: DispatchCommand[] = [];
  171:   const chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[] = [];
  172:   const failed: { occurrenceId: string; tenantId: string; error: unknown }[] = [];
  173:   let unknownEntityType = 0;
  174:   let scanned = 0;
  175:   let partitions = 0;
  176: 
  177:   // Dedup guard: the same occurrence could show up in more than one scanned minute only if
  178:   // materialization ever wrote it under a stale bucket, which shouldn't happen - but a
  179:   // Set guards against double-claiming within a single tick regardless.
  180:   const seen = new Set<string>();
  181: 
  182:   for (const minute of minutesToScan) {
  183:     for (const generation of generations) {
  184:       const partitionKeys = gsi3PartitionsForMinute(minute, generation.shardCount);
  185:       partitions += partitionKeys.length;
  186:       for (const gsi3pk of partitionKeys) {
  187:         const rows = await deps.store.queryGsi3<{ PK: string; SK: string; GSI3SK: string }>({ gsi3pk });
  188:         // PERF-12: this used to be `for (const row of rows)`, one `get`+`transactWrite` pair
  189:         // processed strictly sequentially - see PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY's doc comment for
  190:         // why bounded concurrency replaces that here. `seen`/`claimed`/`failed`/
  191:         // `chasingClaimed`/counters are shared mutable state across concurrent callbacks, but
  192:         // every access happens either synchronously (no `await` in between, so the JS event
  193:         // loop cannot interleave two callbacks' synchronous sections) or as an atomic
  194:         // push/increment - never a race in practice under Node's single-threaded model.
  195:         await mapWithConcurrency(rows, PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY, async (row) => {
  196:           scanned += 1;
  197: 
  198:           // M10 cluster 4: try the chasing shape FIRST (never throws, `undefined` on no
  199:           // match) - the reminder branch below is completely unchanged otherwise.
  200:           const chasingParsed = parseChasingGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
  201:           if (chasingParsed) {
  202:             if (seen.has(chasingParsed.occurrenceId)) return;
  203:             seen.add(chasingParsed.occurrenceId);
  204:             try {
  205:               const outcome = await claimChasingOccurrence(
  206:                 { store: deps.store, tableName: deps.tableName, now: deps.now, claimTtlMs, newEventId: deps.newEventId, correlationId: deps.correlationId },
  207:                 { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
  208:               );
  209:               if (outcome.kind === "CLAIMED") chasingClaimed.push(outcome.command);
  210:               // SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED / LOST_CLAIM_RACE: not failures, same as the reminder path below.
  211:             } catch (err) {
  212:               failed.push({ occurrenceId: chasingParsed.occurrenceId, tenantId: chasingParsed.tenantId, error: err });
  213:             }
  214:             return;
  215:           }
  216: 
  217:           let reminderParsed: { tenantId: string; occurrenceId: string };
  218:           try {
  219:             reminderParsed = parseGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
  220:           } catch {
  221:             // Fail-closed (D-039): neither pattern matched - never process a row we can't
  222:             // identify, never skip it silently either. Alarm-worthy, surfaced via the tick result.
  223:             unknownEntityType += 1;
  224:             return;
  225:           }
  226:           const { tenantId, occurrenceId } = reminderParsed;
  227:           if (seen.has(occurrenceId)) return;
  228:           seen.add(occurrenceId);
  229: 
  230:           try {
  231:             const occurrence = await deps.store.get<ReminderOccurrence>({ PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK });
  232:             if (!occurrence || occurrence.status !== "SCHEDULED") {
  233:               // Already claimed/cancelled/triggered by a prior tick or race - not a failure.
  234:               return;
  235:             }
  236: 
  237:             const claimExpiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) + claimTtlMs).toISOString();
  238:             const newVersion = occurrence.version + 1;
  239:             const now = deps.now();
  240:             // Same value used for both the command's own envelope correlationId (read
  241:             // directly from the SQS body per m5-observability-design.md #2's general SQS
  242:             // rule) and the outbox DomainEvent's correlationId - one business correlation
  243:             // per dispatch, not two independently-generated ids for the same operation.
  244:             const correlationId = deps.correlationId();
  245: 
  246:             const command: DispatchCommand = {
  247:               messageVersion: 1,
  248:               messageId: deps.newEventId(),
  249:               createdAt: now,
  250:               correlationId,
  251:               commandType: "reminder.dispatch.v1",
  252:               tenantId,
  253:               deduplicationKey: `${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${newVersion}`,
  254:               data: {
  255:                 itemId: occurrence.itemId,
  256:                 occurrenceId,
  257:                 occurrenceVersion: newVersion,
  258:                 scheduledAt: occurrence.scheduledAt,
  259:                 itemVersion: occurrence.itemVersion,
  260:                 policyVersion: occurrence.policyVersion,
  261:               },
  262:             };
  263: 
  264:             // M3.5 "DecisÃ£o central: outbox durÃ¡vel": TransactWrite(claim) followed by a
  265:             // direct SendMessage in the handler is NOT atomic (Lambda can die between the
  266:             // two steps, leaving a CLAIMED occurrence with no queued command - neither the
  267:             // producer's own lookback window nor the daily DST reconciliation reliably
  268:             // covers that gap). The fix: write a durable OutboxEvent
  269:             // (destination=SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1) in the SAME transaction as the claim;
  270:             // DispatchOutboxRelay (DynamoDB Streams) publishes it to SQS, a sweeper recovers
  271:             // publication failures. Also set the GSI6 WORKSTATE#CLAIMED pointer so the
  272:             // reconciliation job can find this claim if it expires unrecovered - removed
  273:             // when ReminderDispatch advances to TRIGGERED or reconciliation reverts it.
  274:             const event: DomainEvent = {
  275:               specVersion: "1.0",
  276:               eventId: deps.newEventId(),
  277:               eventType: "ReminderDispatchRequested",
  278:               source: "expiration-tracker.reminder-producer",
  279:               occurredAt: now,
  280:               correlationId,
  281:               tenantId,
  282:               actor: { type: "SYSTEM" },
  283:               aggregate: { type: "ReminderOccurrence", id: occurrenceId, version: newVersion },
  284:               data: command as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
  285:             };
  286:             const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
  287:             appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, event, "SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1");
  288: 
  289:             await deps.store.transactWrite([
  290:               {
  291:                 Update: buildVersionedUpdate({
  292:                   tableName: deps.tableName,
  293:                   key: { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
  294:                   tenantId,
  295:                   expectedVersion: occurrence.version,
  296:                   set: {
  297:                     status: "CLAIMED",
  298:                     claimedAt: deps.now(),
  299:                     claimExpiresAt,
  300:                     GSI6PK: GSI6PK_WORKSTATE_CLAIMED,
  301:                     GSI6SK: buildExpiredClaimGsi6Sk(claimExpiresAt, tenantId, occurrenceId),
  302:                   },
  303:                 }),
  304:               },
  305:               ...outboxEntries,
  306:             ]);
  307: 
  308:             claimed.push(command);
  309:           } catch (err) {
  310:             if (isTransactionCanceled(err)) {
  311:               // Lost the claim race to a concurrent producer tick - not a failure to retry.
  312:               return;
  313:             }
  314:             failed.push({ occurrenceId, tenantId, error: err });
  315:           }
  316:         });
  317:       }
  318:     }
  319:   }
  320: 
  321:   return {
  322:     claimed,
  323:     chasingClaimed,
  324:     failed,
  325:     unknownEntityType,
  326:     scanned,
  327:     minutesScanned: minutesToScan.map((d) => d.toISOString()),
  328:     shardPartitionsScanned: partitions,
  329:   };
  330: }

    1: /**
    2:  * DispatchOutboxRelay + OutboxSweeperReminderDispatch core logic (M3.5,

   10:  *

   12:  * generalizes this from a single hardcoded destination (SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1) to an
   13:  * explicit router keyed by `destination` - a second sweeper querying the SAME global GSI6

   18: import { runWithContext } from "../../shared/observability/context.js";

   22: export const SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1: OutboxDestination = "SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1";
   23: export const SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1: OutboxDestination = "SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1";

   25: /** One sender per recognized destination - a record whose `destination` has no entry here

   27:  * discipline as the single-destination M3.5 version. `tenantId`/`eventType` (BLOCKER-B,

   32:  * they need) simply ignore the two extra arguments. */
   33: export type DestinationSenders = Partial<
   34:   Record<OutboxDestination, (payload: Record<string, unknown>, correlationId: string, tenantId: string, eventType: string) => Promise<void>>
   35: >;

   37: export interface RelayDeps {
   38:   store: OutboxRelayStore;
   39:   senders: DestinationSenders;
   40:   now: () => string;
   41:   leaseOwner: string;
   42:   /** How long a lease is held while attempting SendMessage - default 30s, comfortably
   43:    * longer than one SQS SendMessage call, short enough that a crashed relay invocation's
   44:    * lease is quickly reclaimable by the next relay/sweeper attempt. */
   45:   leaseDurationMs?: number;
   46: }
   47: 
   48: export type PublishOutcome =
   49:   | { kind: "PUBLISHED" }
   50:   | { kind: "SKIPPED_WRONG_DESTINATION" }
   51:   | { kind: "SKIPPED_ALREADY_PUBLISHED" }
   52:   | { kind: "SKIPPED_LEASE_HELD" }
   53:   | { kind: "FAILED"; error: unknown };
   54: 
   55: /** Attempts to publish exactly one outbox record. Never throws for expected outcomes
   56:  * (wrong destination / already published / lease contention) - only for genuinely
   57:  * unexpected failures during acquire/send/mark, surfaced as `FAILED` so the caller (relay
   58:  * Lambda: partial batch failure; sweeper: per-item log+continue) decides retry policy. */
   59: export async function publishOne(deps: RelayDeps, record: OutboxRecord): Promise<PublishOutcome> {
   60:   // Exclusivity (docs/architecture/m3.5-runtime-design.md Â§"DecisÃ£o central"): this relay/
   61:   // sweeper NEVER touches a record it doesn't own the destination for - OutboxPublisher
   62:   // (generic, EventBridge) owns everything else, including records with no `destination`.
   63:   const send = record.destination ? deps.senders[record.destination] : undefined;
   64:   if (!send) {
   65:     return { kind: "SKIPPED_WRONG_DESTINATION" };
   66:   }
   67:   if (record.status === "PUBLISHED") {
   68:     return { kind: "SKIPPED_ALREADY_PUBLISHED" };
   69:   }
   70: 
   71:   // m5-observability-design.md #2: one runWithContext per record - correlationId read from
   72:   // the persisted OutboxRecord (the business operation that originally created it), never
   73:   // from this invocation's own ambient context.
   74:   return runWithContext({ correlationId: outboxRecordCorrelationId(record) }, () => publishAcquiredOrPending(deps, record, send));
   75: }
   76: 
   77: async function publishAcquiredOrPending(
   78:   deps: RelayDeps,
   79:   record: OutboxRecord,
   80:   send: (payload: Record<string, unknown>, correlationId: string, tenantId: string, eventType: string) => Promise<void>,
   81: ): Promise<PublishOutcome> {
   82:   const leaseDurationMs = deps.leaseDurationMs ?? 30_000;
   83:   const now = deps.now();
   84:   const leaseExpiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(now) + leaseDurationMs).toISOString();
   85: 
   86:   const acquired = await deps.store.tryAcquireLease({ PK: record.PK, SK: record.SK }, deps.leaseOwner, leaseExpiresAt, now);
   87:   if (!acquired) {
   88:     return { kind: "SKIPPED_LEASE_HELD" };
   89:   }
   90: 
   91:   try {
   92:     await send(record.payload, outboxRecordCorrelationId(record), record.tenantId, record.eventType);
   93:   } catch (error) {
   94:     // Failure here is expected and recoverable: the lease expires, the sweeper (or a later
   95:     // Stream retry) will retry. A duplicate SendMessage after a retry is absorbed by the
   96:     // downstream worker's own idempotency - never treated as a reason to skip retrying.
   97:     return { kind: "FAILED", error };
   98:   }
   99: 
  100:   // Transition PENDING -> PUBLISHED only AFTER SendMessage confirmed (m3.5-runtime-design.md:
  101:   // "falha entre (2) e (3) Ã© aceitÃ¡vel - duplicata Ã© absorvida pela idempotÃªncia do
  102:   // dispatch"). Failure here also just means the sweeper resends a message that was
  103:   // already delivered once - still recoverable, not a correctness issue.
  104:   await deps.store.markPublished({ PK: record.PK, SK: record.SK });
  105:   return { kind: "PUBLISHED" };
  106: }
  107: 
  108: /** DispatchOutboxRelay / NotificationEmailOutboxRelay entrypoint logic: one call per
  109:  * DynamoDB Streams record (NEW_IMAGE). Which record types actually flow through a given
  110:  * Lambda's Streams filter, and thus which `senders` it needs, is a wiring concern, not this
  111:  * function's - it stays destination-agnostic. */
  112: export async function relayStreamRecord(deps: RelayDeps, record: OutboxRecord): Promise<PublishOutcome> {
  113:   return publishOne(deps, record);
  114: }
  115: 
  116: export interface SweeperDeps extends RelayDeps {
  117:   /** Minimum age (ms) before a PENDING record is swept - covers relay/Stream failure, not
  118:    * normal in-flight latency (m3.5-runtime-design.md: "occurredAt mais antigo que um
  119:    * limiar (2 min)"). */
  120:   minAgeMs?: number;
  121:   pageSize?: number;
  122:   /** Which destinations to sweep this run - the sweeper queries GSI6 once per destination
  123:    * (same global partition, `RECON#OUTBOX#PENDING`, filtered by `destination` server-side by
  124:    * the store). Defaults to every destination this deps' `senders` map recognizes. */
  125:   destinations?: OutboxDestination[];
  126: }
  127: 
  128: export interface SweepResult {
  129:   attempted: number;
  130:   published: number;
  131:   failed: number;
  132:   stillPending: number;
  133: }
  134: 
  135: /** OutboxSweeperReminderDispatch/OutboxSweeperNotificationEmail entrypoint logic: no backoff
  136:  * of its own - every scheduled execution IS one retry attempt (m3.5-runtime-design.md:
  137:  * "nenhum backoff prÃ³prio"). One sweeper instance can cover multiple destinations (M4
  138:  * Â§7.4: "nÃ£o proponho outro GSI nem scan... o sweeper existente deve evoluir para um
  139:  * roteador explÃ­cito por destination"). */
  140: export async function sweepPendingDispatch(deps: SweeperDeps): Promise<SweepResult> {
  141:   const minAgeMs = deps.minAgeMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
  142:   const olderThan = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) - minAgeMs).toISOString();
  143:   const destinations = deps.destinations ?? (Object.keys(deps.senders) as OutboxDestination[]);
  144: 
  145:   let attempted = 0;
  146:   let published = 0;
  147:   let failed = 0;
  148:   let stillPending = 0;
  149: 
  150:   for (const destination of destinations) {
  151:     const candidates = await deps.store.listPendingReminderDispatch({
  152:       destination,
  153:       olderThan,
  154:       pageSize: deps.pageSize,
  155:     });
  156: 
  157:     attempted += candidates.length;
  158:     for (const record of candidates) {
  159:       const outcome = await publishOne(deps, record);
  160:       if (outcome.kind === "PUBLISHED") published += 1;
  161:       else if (outcome.kind === "FAILED") failed += 1;
  162:       else stillPending += 1;
  163:     }
  164:   }
  165: 
  166:   return { attempted, published, failed, stillPending };
  167: }

   18: const MANAGER_ROLES: ReadonlySet<Membership["role"]> = new Set(["OWNER", "ADMIN"]);
   19: 
   20: /** D-201 (MANAGER escalation): same 2-layer eligibility bar as
   21:  * `expiration.ts`'s `buildMemberEligibilityChecker` (Membership ACTIVE AND GlobalUser
   22:  * identityStatus ACTIVE), extended with a role filter - a "manager" is real RBAC
   23:  * (`OWNER`/`ADMIN`), never a separately configured list. */
   24: export function buildTenantManagerLookup(client: DynamoDBDocumentClient, tableName: string): TenantManagerLookup {
   25:   async function isGlobalUserActive(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
   26:     const result = await client.send(new GetCommand({ TableName: tableName, Key: globalUserKey(userId), ConsistentRead: true }));
   27:     return (result.Item as { identityStatus?: string } | undefined)?.identityStatus === "ACTIVE";
   28:   }
   29: 
   30:   return {
   31:     async listActiveManagers(tenantId: string): Promise<{ userId: string }[]> {
   32:       const { PK } = organizationKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity({ tenantId }));
   33:       const result = await client.send(new QueryCommand({ TableName: tableName, ConsistentRead: true, KeyConditionExpression: "PK = :pk AND begins_with(SK, :prefix)", ExpressionAttributeValues: { ":pk": PK, ":prefix": "MEMBER#" } }));
   34:       const candidates = ((result.Items ?? []) as Membership[]).filter((m) => m.status === "ACTIVE" && MANAGER_ROLES.has(m.role));
   35:       const activeFlags = await Promise.all(candidates.map((m) => isGlobalUserActive(m.userId)));
   36:       return candidates.filter((_, i) => activeFlags[i]).map((m) => ({ userId: m.userId }));
   37:     },
   38:     async isActiveManager(tenantId: string, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
   39:       const result = await client.send(new GetCommand({ TableName: tableName, Key: membershipKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity({ tenantId }), userId), ConsistentRead: true }));
   40:       const membership = result.Item as Membership | undefined;
   41:       if (membership?.status !== "ACTIVE" || !MANAGER_ROLES.has(membership.role)) return false;
   42:       return isGlobalUserActive(userId);
   43:     },
   44:   };
   45: }

   77: ## Required change 4: rollback/roll-forward ordering â€” explicit gates, not implied sequencing
   78: 
   79: **Rollback**, restated as a strict, named sequence:
   80: 1. Terraform apply: both event-source-mappings' `enabled = false`.
   81: 2. **Gate**: poll `aws lambda get-event-source-mapping` (via the `claude-dev` profile, per this
   82:    repo's existing AWS-verification convention) for BOTH mappings until `State == "Disabled"`
   83:    (AWS's own documented terminal state, distinct from the transitional `Disabling` â€” confirmed
   84:    via AWS Lambda's `UpdateEventSourceMapping`/`GetEventSourceMapping` API reference this round,
   85:    Codex's own citation). Do NOT start the quiescence timer on apply-success alone.
   86: 3. **Gate**: 90-second bounded wait (unchanged number/reasoning from round 5) starts only after
   87:    step 2's poll confirms both `Disabled`.
   88: 4. Terraform apply: `SCAN_MODE = "LEGACY"`.
   89: 
   90: **Roll-forward** (new/re-enable â€” not previously given its own explicit gate order, added this
   91: round): 1. Terraform apply: bump `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` to `N+1` (deployed as a Lambda environment
   92: variable change, same mechanism as `SCAN_MODE` itself) â€” this MUST land before step 2, so anything
   93: that starts matching from step 2 onward is unambiguously post-bump. 2. Terraform apply:
   94: `SCAN_MODE = "PAGED"`. 3. Terraform apply: both mappings' `enabled = true`. Any message left queued
   95: from before the rollback (necessarily stamped with epoch â‰¤ N, since nothing could stamp `N+1`
   96: before step 1 completed) is now provably stale the instant a handler reads it under the new
   97: `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH = N+1` â€” closing required change 3's residual-message concern with the exact
   98: ordering guarantee Codex asked for, not just the comparison mechanism alone.
   99: 
  100: ## Self-grade (Claude, blind â€” before seeing Codex round 6)
  101: 
  102: **9.3/10.** All 4 fixes are narrow, mechanical, and each traces to a specific Codex citation with
  103: no new structural surface introduced (round 5's own critique confirmed 3 of 4 items were
  104: "conceptually closed, integration incomplete" â€” this round is exactly that integration, not a new
  105: idea). The one piece I'd flag as still worth a skeptical read: the `data.data` nesting in the event
  106: schema (an `SqsCommandEnvelope` embedded inside a `DomainEvent`'s `data` field, itself containing
  107: ANOTHER `data`) is verbose and easy to get subtly wrong in a real Ajv schema file â€” it's correct by
  108: construction (matches `producer.ts`'s own existing double-nesting exactly) but worth the
  109: implementer writing the actual schema file carefully rather than trusting this doc's prose
  110: one-for-one.

Achados bloqueantes reais: (1) o próprio wrapper fenced se autocontradiz — não consegue escrever `DELETING`/`DELETED` nem permitir o create inicial sob a mesma regra "exige ACTIVE"; (2) bootstrap do primeiro tenant quebrado — `resolve-request-context.ts` cria `IdentityMapping` antes de qualquer checagem de lifecycle; (3) a regra de enforcement proposta via `dependency-cruiser` é tecnicamente inviável (só analisa grafo de imports, não construção AST) — precisa ser ESLint; (4) inventário "19 arquivos" errado (são 14) e incompleto mesmo assim — escritores S3/SQS/Step Functions diretos ficam fora da superfície DynamoDB coberta; (5) janela do protocolo "claim antes do efeito" para SES/Bedrock/Textract é de minutos, não milissegundos, e o código real do Bedrock ignora deliberadamente um erro de quota já reservada; (6) URLs presignadas são emitidas depois da escrita fenced em `GuestSubmissionService.startSubmission`/`ImportService.reserveImport`, não antes; (7) sem prova de descoberta/limpeza de objeto S3 tardio após convergência. Uma entrada cujo `PK` não casa com o padrão `TENANT#` (as exceções listadas acima) continua sem verificação — gap residual, documentado explicitamente no cabeçalho do arquivo e coberto por teste dedicado nomeando-o como tal, não mascarado. Isso NÃO é uma prova estrutural completa (uma entidade global futura roteada erroneamente por esta lane sem `TENANT#` prefix nem `tenantId` declarado ainda passaria), mas fecha especificamente o cenário que D-075/Codex round-2 apontou como o achado mais sério: `Item.tenantId` forjado para bater com a fence enquanto o `PK` real aponta para outro tenant agora É pego, antes de qualquer `transactWrite`. **IMPLEMENTED + UNIT TESTED** (4 testes novos em `test/unit/tenant-lifecycle.test.ts`: Put com `Item.tenantId` correto mas `PK` de outro tenant rejeitado; Update com `PK` de outro tenant rejeitado; `TableName` divergente rejeitado; teste do gap residual reescrito para nomear explicitamente que é um cenário diferente do gap agora fechado, não o mesmo). 1026 testes de backend passando (era 1023), typecheck/lint/check-boundaries/check-docs limpos, zero regressão | Type 1 (nível 5-6, `AGENTS.md` §4 — fechamento de achado de segurança/modelo de dados sinalizado por revisão adversarial anterior) | N/A — fechamento mecânico de achado já escopado por D-075, protocolo completo não reaberto | N/A (terceira rodada Codex agendada para depois do item 2 desta mesma sessão) | **IMPLEMENTED + UNIT TESTED** — gap do PK/TableName fechado para toda entidade cuja chave segue a convenção `TENANT#<id>#...` (universal no modelo de dados atual); gap residual para entidades não-`TENANT#`-prefixed (nenhuma roteada por esta lane hoje) documentado explicitamente, não mascarado | `src/shared/tenant-lifecycle/tenant-business-mutation.ts`, `test/unit/tenant-lifecycle.test.ts` | 2026-08-29 |

mais 3 refinamentos não-bloqueantes incorporados (ordem corrigida no contrato do `CloseOrganizationService` — checagem de estado terminal ANTES do retry incondicional, não depois; `retryCount` nomeado como constante em vez de literal mágico; O único precedente real de bloqueio (Jira) se aplica a hard DELETE de usuário, operação mais destrutiva sem equivalente direto neste projeto. **Decisão diverge deliberadamente do mercado** (não por convergência externa, registrado explicitamente como tal) — justificada pela natureza do domínio (rastreamento de prazo/obrigação legal tem custo de item órfão mais alto que um board de tarefas genérico). **Achado interno decisivo**: `assigneeUserId` não tem GSI próprio, mas `GSI1` (`GSI1PK=TENANT#t#ITEMSTATUS#ACTIVE`, `projection_type=ALL`, confirmado por leitura direta de `infra/modules/dynamo-table/main.tf`) já é o índice que o dashboard usa para listar itens ACTIVE de um tenant — encontrar "itens ACTIVE atribuídos ao usuário X" é uma `Query` nesse índice já aprovado + `FilterExpression`, zero GSI novo, zero decisão D-026 nova. `ItemWatch` (sem índice viável, precedente B2B-11 de "remover watcher é sempre seguro") e `RequirementAssignment`/`TrackedSubject` (confirmado por leitura que nenhum dos dois tem um segundo campo de responsável) ficam fora de escopo. **Rodada 1 (Codex 7,0/10 design, 7,2/10 régua contestada, não aprovado)**: síntese da pesquisa Jira imprecisa (citava só o ticket antigo, não a distinção real deactivate-preserva vs. delete-bloqueia); TOCTOU real e não resolvido entre o check via GSI1 (eventualmente consistente, nunca `ConsistentRead` em GSI) e a transação de remoção; checklist original subpesava consistência sob concorrência; capacidade por tenant não fechada. **Rodada 2 (Codex 8,1/10 design, 8,4/10 régua, não aprovado)**: pesquisa Jira corrigida (deactivate preserva, delete bloqueia — fontes `support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/remove-or-suspend-a-user/` + thread da comunidade, ambas fetch direto); TOCTOU aceito como best-effort explicitamente *bounded* pelo status quo já `APPROVED` em B2B-11 (pior caso nunca pior que o bug que esta proposta corrige) — atomicidade perfeita confirmada inatingível (GSI nunca fortemente consistente, `TransactWriteItems` exige chaves conhecidas antecipadamente, máx. 100 itens); checklist reancorado com critério novo dedicado a consistência (peso 25%, contestado de novo por premiar demais uma garantia fraca); payload do erro limitado a 20 `itemId`s + `totalKnown`/`truncated`; decidido "sem bypass de emergência nesta versão" como default normativo (não mais pendência aberta). **Rodada 3 (Codex 9,2/10 régua, 9,1/10 design, Claude 9,1/10, APROVADO)**: critério de consistência repesado (25%→15%, âncora exige declaração explícita de semântica best-effort + observabilidade via mecanismos JÁ existentes — audit event de remoção + log de cancelamento de notificação de B2B-11 — nunca telemetria nova inventada); contrato de paginação explícito fechando risco real de falso negativo (`Query` pagina a partição `GSI1` `ACTIVE` inteira via `LastEvaluatedKey` até esgotar, nunca usa `Limit` do DynamoDB como truncamento — o cap de 20 vale só para a lista retornada, depois de já contar o total real); precisão de citação (conclusão vem da combinação de 2 fontes, não de uma isolada). **Mecanismo decidido**: precondição bloqueante *best-effort* (nunca atômica) em `RemoveMembershipService.remove()`/`LeaveOrganizationService.leave()`, via porta nova `AssignedActiveItemsLookup` no módulo `organization` (implementação real no composition root, mesma classe de decisão já `APPROVED` de `MemberEligibilityChecker`/B2B-11) — nota de implementação do Codex: o `queryGsi1` já existente em `dynamodb-expiration-store.ts` tem `Limit`+break por `items.length`, não deve ser reaproveitado ingenuamente para este lookup. Erro novo `ResponsibilityReassignmentRequiredError` (`BUSINESS_RULE`, `retryable: false`, mesmo padrão de `LastOwnerError`) com `{targetUserId, itemIds (até 20), totalKnown, truncated}`. `ItemWatch` fora de escopo. Sem bypass de emergência nesta versão. **Fora de escopo desta rodada**: implementação real (nenhum código escrito) — só o mecanismo/design, mesmo padrão de D-121. | Type 1 (nível 5, `AGENTS.md` §4 — nova fronteira de módulo cruzando organization↔expiration, nova precondição bloqueante numa mutação já em produção) | 9,1/10 (Rodada 3, auto-avaliação às cegas) | 9,1/10 (Rodada 3, final) | **DESIGN APROVADO — implementação real (nova porta, novo erro, wiring do composition root, suíte de testes) fica para uma sessão dedicada futura, mesmo padrão de D-121** | `docs/architecture/reviews/responsibility-reassignment-scoping/` | 2026-08-30 |
