Estende `src/modules/document-archive/`: `domain/requirement.ts` (`applicability` fato persistido nunca derivado, `evidenceVersionId` singular, `deriveRequirementStatus` pura — MISSING/PENDING/SATISFIED/NOT_SATISFIED/NOT_APPLICABLE — e `isRequirementExpiringSoon` como subdivisão de leitura de SATISFIED, nunca persistida, mesma janela de 7 dias de `frontend/src/api/presentation.ts`'s `presentItemUrgency`/`SOON_THRESHOLD_DAYS`), `application/document-archive-service.ts` (createRequirement/getRequirement/listRequirements/updateRequirement/linkEvidence/unlinkEvidence/deleteRequirement, todas via `authorize()`), `http/` (7 rotas novas), 5 schemas JSON novos, worker diário `src/workers/requirement-reindex/` + handler dedicado (EventBridge Scheduler, `cron(0 4 * * ? *)`, mesmo padrão de `tenant-purge-sweep.ts`). **Desvio real do design original, documentado (não escondido)**: `Requirement` denormaliza `evidenceDocumentId`/`evidenceSeq`/`evidenceState`/`evidenceValidUntil` junto de `evidenceVersionId` no momento do link, em vez de resolver a DocumentVersion via `versionLookupGsi5Keys` (AP11, reservado exatamente para isso na Decisão 2) — esse par de atributos GSI5PK/GSI5SK já é usado, de forma esparsa, pelo índice de fila de revisão (`reviewQueueGsi5Keys`) e é REMOVIDO no exato momento em que uma version chega a `ACCEPTED`, o único estado que um Requirement realmente precisa localizar. Ocupar o mesmo par permanentemente quebraria a fila de revisão; a denormalização evita o conflito sem tocar o contrato existente do GSI5, e também permite ao worker diário e a `updateRequirement` (numa mudança de `applicability`) re-derivar `status` sem nenhuma leitura extra. `linkEvidence` por isso recebe `documentId` explicitamente do chamador em vez de resolver a partir de `versionId` sozinho — sinalizado aqui como questão em aberto para quem implementar guest access/recorrência, caso um fluxo futuro precise de "link por versionId apenas". **RBAC**: novas actions `docarchive:requirement-create/read/update/delete`, deliberadamente não reaproveitando as actions `requirement:*` já existentes (`identity/domain/authorization.ts`) — aquelas pertencem ao conceito mais antigo `RequirementAssignment` do módulo `subject`, um agregado distinto (vinculado a `ExpirationItem`, não a `DocumentVersion`); a colisão de nome foi resolvida deliberadamente, nunca reaproveitada silenciosamente. **G-V3 confirmado ao vivo**: branch `NOT_APPLICABLE` de `deriveRequirementStatus` (mutação removendo o `if` derrubou o teste correspondente, revertida); Rejeitada (c) pura (não fazer nada): a rota já aceita um `documentType` explícito sem nunca validá-lo contra o catálogo — lacuna de integridade referencial real e corrigível sem quebrar nada. **E-014 SIM PARCIAL**, checklist com 4 critérios pesados somando 100% (C1 30% nunca quebra tráfego que hoje funciona sem o campo; C2 25% só valida valor que o próprio chamador forneceu, na primeira execução real de cada `idempotencyKey`; C3 30% nenhuma resposta distingue causa interna para chamador não autenticado, aplicação local de [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457); C4 15% obrigatoriedade plena só avança depois de existir mecanismo de descoberta, ancorado em [Martin Fowler — Parallel Change](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ParallelChange.html)) — Rodada 1 citou fontes desatualizadas/sem peso (RFC 7807, Stripe fora de contexto), corrigido na Rodada 2/3 com URLs+data de acesso+pesos. **Achado real da Rodada 2 do Codex, resolvido explicitamente na Rodada 3**: `existingReplay` (lookup por `idempotencyKey`) roda ANTES de qualquer validação de payload — propriedade PRÉ-EXISTENTE do mecanismo (D-143 Decision 4, `fileName` também nunca foi revalidado num replay), não uma lacuna nova. Decisão: manter essa ordem — `idempotencyKey` identifica uma operação lógica, a primeira execução real de um dado key fixa o resultado, uma repetição do mesmo key com `documentType` diferente (mesmo inválido) devolve o snapshot original; C2 formalmente redefinido para cobrir só a primeira execução real. CRITIQUE

1. `:leaseNow` placeholder and ISO comparison — CONFIRMED.

`occ.ts` reserves `:now` for `updatedAt` and rejects collisions during `extraConditions` merging ([occ.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/shared/dynamodb/occ.ts:85), [occ.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/shared/dynamodb/occ.ts:130)). Round 6’s distinct `:leaseNow` therefore fixes the actual failure.

The value representation is also sound. The lease design persists `leaseUntil` as an ISO timestamp and uses it in the lexically ordered GSI6 sort key ([round-4-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-4-claude-revision.md:37)). With both operands produced in the canonical `Date.prototype.toISOString()` UTC format, DynamoDB string comparison for `leaseUntil >= :leaseNow` preserves chronological order. A real implementation should reuse the invocation’s injected/captured ISO `now` rather than call `new Date()` independently, but that is a testability/detail refinement, not a correctness gap in this plan.

2. Event→queue wire shape — CONFIRMED.

The claimed precedent is exact:

- `producer.ts` creates the complete `DispatchCommand`, including both envelope and inner `data` fields ([producer.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/workers/reminder-producer/producer.ts:246)).
- It assigns that complete command directly to the domain event’s `data` ([producer.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/workers/reminder-producer/producer.ts:274), [producer.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/workers/reminder-producer/producer.ts:284)).
- The outbox persists `event.data` as `record.payload` ([outbox.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts:140)).
- The relay forwards `record.payload` unchanged ([relay.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.ts:91)).
- The generic SQS sender serializes that same payload directly ([reminder.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/runtime/aws/composition/reminder.ts:140), [reminder.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/runtime/aws/composition/reminder.ts:144)).

Consequently, Round 6’s outer domain-event `data` containing a complete `SqsCommandEnvelope`, whose own `data` contains the continuation fields, produces the intended `data.data` structure and the correct SQS body end to end. Its proposed event-side and queue-side schema shapes match the repository’s existing `allOf` envelope pattern ([command-envelope.v1.json](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/schemas/queues/command-envelope.v1.json:6), [reminder-dispatch.v1.json](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/schemas/queues/reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6)).

3. `rolloutEpoch`, including reconciliation reclaim — CONFIRMED.

Round 6 explicitly requires `rolloutEpoch` in both schemas and names every emission path: fresh acquire, ordinary reclaim, reconciliation `SCANLEASE` reclaim, and continuation checkpoint ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:61)).

Crucially, it does not merely imply reconciliation access: it explicitly says the new reconciliation pass reads `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` and that the reconciliation Lambda configuration must receive that additional environment variable ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:66)). The current Terraform supplies that Lambda only `local.common_env` ([main.tf](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/infra/main.tf:298), [main.tf](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/infra/main.tf:305)), so the plan clearly identifies a real wiring change rather than assuming the variable already exists. A competent implementation can add it to that module’s environment variables and inject the parsed value through the handler/composition boundary without guessing.

4. Rollback/roll-forward ordering — CONFIRMED.

Rollback now has the required strict gates: disable both mappings, poll both until terminal `Disabled`, start the 90-second quiescence interval only afterward, and only then deploy `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:79)). AWS confirms that `Enabled=false` pauses polling and invocation, supporting this gate semantics. [AWS Lambda API documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/api/API_UpdateEventSourceMapping.html)

Roll-forward likewise states the safety-critical ordering explicitly: deploy epoch `N+1`, deploy `PAGED`, then enable either mapping ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:90)). Therefore pre-rollback residual messages cannot become valid after re-enable.

SCORE: 9.3/10

Round 6 closes all four remaining required changes. The plan has converged above the protocol gate and is sufficiently precise for implementation without architectural guesswork.

- The generic SQS sender serializes that same payload directly ([reminder.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/runtime/aws/composition/reminder.ts:140), [reminder.ts](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/src/runtime/aws/composition/reminder.ts:144)).

Consequently, Round 6’s outer domain-event `data` containing a complete `SqsCommandEnvelope`, whose own `data` contains the continuation fields, produces the intended `data.data` structure and the correct SQS body end to end. Its proposed event-side and queue-side schema shapes match the repository’s existing `allOf` envelope pattern ([command-envelope.v1.json](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/schemas/queues/command-envelope.v1.json:6), [reminder-dispatch.v1.json](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/schemas/queues/reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6)).

3. `rolloutEpoch`, including reconciliation reclaim — CONFIRMED.

Round 6 explicitly requires `rolloutEpoch` in both schemas and names every emission path: fresh acquire, ordinary reclaim, reconciliation `SCANLEASE` reclaim, and continuation checkpoint ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:61)).

Crucially, it does not merely imply reconciliation access: it explicitly says the new reconciliation pass reads `SCAN_MODE_EPOCH` and that the reconciliation Lambda configuration must receive that additional environment variable ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:66)). The current Terraform supplies that Lambda only `local.common_env` ([main.tf](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/infra/main.tf:298), [main.tf](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/infra/main.tf:305)), so the plan clearly identifies a real wiring change rather than assuming the variable already exists. A competent implementation can add it to that module’s environment variables and inject the parsed value through the handler/composition boundary without guessing.

4. Rollback/roll-forward ordering — CONFIRMED.

Rollback now has the required strict gates: disable both mappings, poll both until terminal `Disabled`, start the 90-second quiescence interval only afterward, and only then deploy `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:79)). AWS confirms that `Enabled=false` pauses polling and invocation, supporting this gate semantics. [AWS Lambda API documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/api/API_UpdateEventSourceMapping.html)

Roll-forward likewise states the safety-critical ordering explicitly: deploy epoch `N+1`, deploy `PAGED`, then enable either mapping ([round-6-claude-revision.md](C:/Users/Usuario/Desktop/projects/expiration-tracker/docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-implementation-plan-scoping/round-6-claude-revision.md:90)). Therefore pre-rollback residual messages cannot become valid after re-enable.

SCORE: 9.3/10

Round 6 closes all four remaining required changes. The plan has converged above the protocol gate and is sufficiently precise for implementation without architectural guesswork.
